samples.question: This picture shows one large square panel with a solid dark border. Inside the border the panel is a lattice of 12 rows and 12 columns of equal square cells, separated by thin coloured rules; number the rows 1 to 12 from the top and the columns 1 to 12 from the left. Every cell is filled with a single flat shade, and exactly three shades are used in the whole panel: a light one, a middle one and a dark one. All three shades appear many times, so 'darker' always means darker than another cell of the same panel and never darker than some fixed outside standard. Four coloured notches on the border, one on each side, mark the panel's horizontal and vertical centre lines; they cross at the panel's centre point, which is the corner where the four middle cells meet. Carry out this operation. Turn the panel a half turn, 180 degrees, about that centre point, so that the cell in row r and column c lands on the cell in row 13 minus r and column 13 minus c. Now look only at the upper half of the panel, its rows 1 to 6, and mark every cell there that is strictly darker in shade than the cell it lands on, that is the cell in row 13 minus r and column 13 minus c. Leave a cell unmarked when the two shades are equal and when the landing cell is the darker one. The marks form a pattern on a lattice 12 cells wide and 6 cells tall, and that pattern is always exactly one of six figures. 'cross' is a wide horizontal bar two rows thick across the middle with a two-cell wide vertical bar through the middle running the full height. 'tee' is a solid two-row bar along the top with a two-cell wide vertical bar hanging from its middle. 'ell' is a three-cell wide vertical bar down the left side with a solid two-row bar along the bottom. 'ring' is a hollow rectangle: solid top and bottom rows and single-cell left and right sides. 'ex' is two full diagonals crossing. 'arrow' is a chevron whose two arms meet at the bottom middle and continue as a short two-cell wide stem. The figure is drawn nowhere in the picture. Each pair of compared cells straddles both centre lines, so no half of the panel contains a single complete pair and neither half alone rules out any figure. The three shades are used exactly 48 times each in the panel and exactly 24 times each in the upper half, so shade area, cell counts, colours, sizes and positions are the same for every answer. Which figure do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: arrow, cross, ell, ex, ring, tee.
